title: Effects of Trunk Exercise on Trunk Control and Balance in Persons With Stroke
brief_summary: This study examined the effects of trunk exercise on unstable surfaces on trunk control and balance for persons in the sub-acute stage of stroke. The hypothesis was that, compared to upper limb exercises in well supported sitting position, this exercise would lead to better trunk control and sitting and standing balance. The results supported the hypothesis.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* age: between 20-80 years old
* first time stroke
* could sit without back support at least 20 seconds
* could understand and follow experimental instructions

Exclusion Criteria:

* medically unstable
* other neuromuscular/musculoskeletal problems that would affect balance
